en: Michele, it is so fantastic to have you here today.
zh: Michele，今天能邀请到你真是太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for having me.

en: So you started working with Replit in 2022.

en: A lot has happened since then.

en: Can you walk me through what the product was in 2022?

en: Who was it for?
zh: 它是为谁设计的？

speaker: Unknown
en: What did the product look like?
zh: 产品当时看起来是什么样子的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, you know, I want to get to sort of 2024, but what was it like four years ago?
zh: 然后，你知道，我想聊到 2024 年的情况，但四年前它是什么样子的？

speaker: Unknown
en: So Replit started in 2016.
zh: 所以 Replit 成立于 2016 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: Up to 2023, it was a cloud development environment.
zh: 直到 2023 年，它是一个云开发环境。

speaker: Unknown
en: We made it as easy as possible for developers to kickstart their code on our platform.
zh: 我们尽可能让开发者在我们平台上轻松启动他们的代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: In reality, though, we were building an amazing platform that eventually allowed us to build Replit Agent.
zh: 但实际上，我们正在建立一个惊人的平台，最终让我们能够构建 Replit Agent。

speaker: Unknown
en: And tell me about Replit Agent.
zh: 跟我说说 Replit Agent 吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where did that idea come from?
zh: 这个想法是哪里来的？

speaker: Unknown
en: When did you guys start working on Replit Agent?
zh: 你们什么时候开始研发 Replit Agent 的？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I would say there was always the vision, in a sense.
zh: 所以我想说这在某种意义上一直是一个愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you go back and check the slide decks that Amjad, the CEO and co-founder of Replit, was using to raise money, he always had in mind something that looked like Replit Agent, where AI would have generated the code for our users, and in turn, our users would have focused on business ideas and literally what is crucial about running a business rather than the code required to create products.
zh: 如果你回去查看 Replit 的 CEO 和联合创始人 Amjad 用来融资的幻灯片，他心里一直有一个类似 Replit Agent 的东西，AI 会为我们的用户生成代码，反过来，我们的用户将专注于商业想法，以及字面上经营业务的关键所在，而不是创造产品所需的代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: It took a while to get there, and not only because it took a while to build Replit, but because the entire field of AI was growing really fast at the time, but maybe we were not expecting that to happen, in a sense, so quickly.
zh: 到达那里花了很长时间，不仅因为构建 Replit 需要时间，而且因为当时整个 AI 领域发展非常快，但也许我们在某种意义上并没有预料到那会这么快发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that buildup, I would say, started around 2020.
zh: 而那种积累，我想说，开始于 2020 年左右。

speaker: Unknown
en: when we got access to the first token source models like GPT-2 from OpenAI.
zh: 当时我们获得了第一批 token 源模型，比如来自 OpenAI 的 GPT-2。

speaker: Unknown
en: Back in those days, I was a researcher at Stanford, so I was very early on LLMs applied to source code, and it was exactly the same bet that basically Rapid was making.
zh: 在那些日子里，我是斯坦福大学的研究员，所以我非常早地接触到了应用于源代码的 LLM，这基本上和 Rapid 所做的赌注完全一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I did it from a research point of view.
zh: 我是从研究的角度做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Rapid was doing that from a product point of view.
zh: Rapid 是从产品的角度做那件事的。

speaker: Unknown
en: we met halfway.
zh: 我们在中间相遇了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I met Amjad in 2021.
zh: 所以我在 2021 年遇到了 Amjad。

speaker: Unknown
en: I showed him a demo of something that looked like Replication, but way more primitive compared to what we launched.
zh: 我向他展示了一个看起来像 Replication 的演示，但与我们发布的版本相比要原始得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we realized we had exactly the same life mission.
zh: 我们意识到我们有完全相同的人生使命。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow, okay, so you were doing research in this space, and Amjad had this sort of very similar vision of what the future should look like.
zh: 哇，好吧，所以你在这个领域做研究，而 Amjad 对未来的样子也有这种非常相似的愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: You guys came together and were like, wow, this is just a match made in heaven.
zh: 你们走到一起，就像，哇，这简直是天作之合。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you joined immediately as president and head of AI, or what was sort of the journey there?
zh: 然后你立即作为总裁兼 AI 负责人加入，或者那里的过程是怎样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: The journey was I joined to build the AI team zero to one, basically.
zh: 过程就是我加入是为了从零到一组建 AI 团队，基本上是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my only fixation was to create something like Replicit Agent.
zh: 我唯一的执念就是创建像 Replicit Agent 这样的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I recall, I think, maybe two weeks after I officially joined, I wrote a manifesto, like an AI manifesto for the company.
zh: 我记得，我想是在我正式加入大约两周后，我写了一份宣言，像是公司的 AI 宣言。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you go back and read it today, it basically describes what not only we launched with Replicit Agent v1 back in September 2024.
zh: 如果你回去读它今天的内容，它基本上描述了不仅我们在 2024 年 9 月发布的 Replicit Agent v1 中推出的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: The reason why I wrote it is because
zh: 我写它的原因是因为

speaker: Unknown
en: I realized, and also the reason why I joined the company, to be honest, because I realized they built an amazing platform where all the tools necessary to actually build an agent were already in place.
zh: 我意识到了，这也是我加入公司的原因，老实说，因为我意识到他们建立了一个惊人的平台，所有实际构建智能体所需的工具都已经就位了。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think about it, what an AI agent does, especially for coding, is to use the same tools that we built for developers in the past, and it just learns how to orchestrate them correctly as if it was a human developer.
zh: 如果你想想看，AI 智能体做什么，特别是对于编码来说，就是使用我们过去为开发者构建的相同工具，它只是学习如何正确编排它们，就像它是一个人类开发者一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: So everything was there, and I told myself...
zh: 所以一切都已经存在了，我告诉自己……

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd rather join a team that knows exactly how to build that, is already very advanced in terms of engineering culture and loves exactly the same problem I want to work on, rather than trying to raise money once again and build the right team and make mistakes because early stage is very probable to make mistakes in creating the right team.
zh: 我宁愿加入一个确切知道如何构建那个东西的团队，在工程文化方面已经非常先进，并且热爱我想解决的完全相同的问题，而不是试图再次筹集资金、组建合适的团队并犯错，因为在早期阶段在创建合适的团队时犯错是非常可能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to talk about what it was like to launch Replit Agent, because I'm sure that was a magical moment.
zh: 我想谈谈推出 Replit Agent 是什么样的，因为我确信那是一个神奇的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: But before we do that, I'm so curious.
zh: 但在我们这样做之前，我非常好奇。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's always very interesting how companies think about when to invest in a bet and structure their teams around a bet or something that they don't know is going to work versus when to continue investing in the thing that maybe it's not full product market fit, but it seems to be working in some sense.
zh: 我认为公司如何考虑何时投资于一个赌注并围绕一个赌注或他们不知道是否会成功的东西来构建他们的团队，或者何时继续投资于那个可能还没有完全产品市场契合度，但在某种意义上似乎正在起作用的东西，总是非常有趣的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what was the structure of the team?
zh: 所以团队的结构是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: How many people were working on Replit Agent?
zh: 有多少人在从事 Replit Agent 的工作？

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you guys make that happen?
zh: 你们是如何做到的？

speaker: Unknown
en: I would love to tell you that it was just one of the many bets.
zh: 我很想告诉你这只是众多赌注中的一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if it didn't pan out, everything would have been all right.
zh: 如果没有成功，一切都会没事的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The truth is pretty much the opposite.
zh: 事实恰恰相反。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we're almost not at the finish line of the company because we had money in the bank.
zh: 我想我们还没到公司的终点线，因为我们在银行里有资金。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the product we built up to there was not easy to monetize.
zh: 但是我们在那之前构建的产品并不容易变现。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was amazing for the educational markets.
zh: 它在教育领域非常出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: So schools across the globe used us.
zh: 所以全球的学校都在使用我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why our user base was growing so fast.
zh: 这就是我们的用户基数增长如此之快的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it was hard for us to justify, you know, the growth of the company, our valuation, and basically becoming what we are today.
zh: 但是我们很难证明,你知道,公司的发展,我们的估值,以及基本上成为今天这个样子的合理性。

speaker: Unknown
en: So RapidAgent was both a bet that matched our company mission, which is empowering the next billion software creators.
zh: 所以 RapidAgent 既是一个符合我们公司使命的赌注,即赋能下一个十亿软件创作者。

speaker: Unknown
en: but also a necessity.
zh: 但也是一种必需。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had to find strong product market feed that allowed us to grow to where we are today.
zh: 我们必须找到强大的产品市场反馈,让我们能够发展到今天这个地步。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it started as a small group of misfits.
zh: 它起初是一小群不合群的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I created a very small AI team, and I told them, regardless of where this goes,
zh: 所以我组建了一个非常小的 AI 团队,我告诉他们,不管这会走向何方,

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's try to build this.
zh: 让我们试着去构建它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's try to show the world how this new technology is going to look like.
zh: 让我们试着向世界展示这项新技术将是什么样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's build something for non-developers, because it's going to be highly differentiated, and it's a much harder technical problem, to be honest.
zh: 让我们为非开发者构建一些东西,因为这将具有高度的差异化,而且说实话,这是一个更难的技术问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the last two months before launching, more than half of the company was working on RapidAgent full-time.
zh: 我认为在发布前的最后两个月,公司超过一半的人都在全职从事 RapidAgent 的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how many people?
zh: 所以有多少人?

speaker: Unknown
en: That was about maybe 60 people, 30 people?
zh: 那大概是 60 人,30 人吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: It was 30 people, roughly.
zh: 大概是 30 人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were down to like a skeleton team.
zh: 我们缩减到了像骨干团队一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say more than 80% of the company was technical.
zh: 我会说公司超过 80% 是技术人员。

speaker: Unknown
en: All the other functions were run like part-time by some of us.
zh: 所有其他的职能都是由我们中的一些人兼职负责的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then once we had problem market fits and we sat on that for a while when we realized, okay, this is actually working well, then we started to grow the account again.
zh: 然后一旦我们有了问题市场契合,我们坚持了一段时间,当我们意识到,好吧,这实际上运作良好,然后我们又开始增加账户。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow.
zh: 哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: So right before launch, it seems like it was probably kind of like a hard time for the company then.
zh: 所以就在发布之前,那对公司来说可能是一段相当艰难的时期。

speaker: Unknown
en: You sort of scaled down.
zh: 你们确实缩减了规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: Darkest possible times.
zh: 最黑暗的时期。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Describe that for me.
zh: 为我描述一下那个时期。

speaker: Unknown
en: What did that feel like coming into work every day?
zh: 每天来上班是什么感觉?

speaker: Unknown
en: So early 2024, we attempted to sell the product to the enterprise, the previous one, not Rapid Agent.
zh: 所以 2024 年初,我们尝试将产品卖给企业,之前的产品,不是 Rapid Agent。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we found a lot of interest in terms of the philosophy of our product.
zh: 我们发现对我们产品的理念有很大的兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything integrated, one single place where you can go from idea to creating your software.
zh: 所有东西集成在一起,一个单一的地方,你可以从想法到创建你的软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: but very hard to actually have companies embrace it, because it would have displaced a lot of different tools.
zh: 但是实际上很难让公司接受它,因为它会取代很多不同的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as you know, every developer has a love for their own specific tools, and it would have been really hard to tell them, drop everything, just embrace Rabbit.
zh: 而你知道,每个开发者都对自己特定的工具有热爱,如果告诉他们放弃一切,只接受 Rabbit,那真的很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we sort of hit that dead end and then we went in quick order.
zh: 所以我们碰到了那个死胡同,然后我们迅速行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: We relocated away from San Francisco down in Foster City.
zh: 我们从旧金山搬迁到了福斯特城。

speaker: Unknown
en: So brand new, much bigger office.
zh: 所以全新的,更大的办公室。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had to go through a layoff because our sales and marketing team was not, first of all, not required at that point in time because we didn't have anything to sell.
zh: 我们不得不进行裁员,因为我们的销售和营销团队不再,首先,不再需要了,因为那时我们没有任何东西可卖。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also they were there with a different product in mind.
zh: 而且他们也是带着不同的产品想法在那里的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And six months ahead of us, where we just knew we had a deadline that I dropped on everyone's calendar, I said, this is the day where we're going to be launching Reputation V1.
zh: 而在我们前面六个月,我们只是知道我们有一个我扔在每个人日历上的截止日期,我说,这是我们要发布 Reputation V1 的日子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything else was just us showing up at the office every single day, heads down, knowing that we had this bet that must have worked by then.
zh: 其他的一切都只是我们每天出现在办公室,埋头苦干,知道我们有一个必须在那时成功的赌注。

speaker: Unknown
en: It required a lot of grit and determination to actually go through all of that.
zh: 穿过所有这一切需要大量的毅力和决心。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think it gave us an opportunity to be extremely focused.
zh: 但我认为这给了我们一个极度专注的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I never experienced that again, because since the launch, when we actually hit product market fit, my life changed completely.
zh: 我再也没有经历过那种感觉,因为自从发布以来,当我们真正达到产品市场契合时,我的生活完全改变了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't spend every single second of my life thinking about the technical problem.
zh: 我不再花费生命中的每一秒思考技术问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now I have way more duties.
zh: 现在我有更多的职责。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I don't regret that.
zh: 我并不后悔。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's a lot of fun.
zh: 我认为这很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm learning a lot of new skills with that.
zh: 我正在借此学习很多新技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it will never come back again.
zh: 但它永远不会回来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those six months were both peak productivity and also maybe peak determination for us because we had to make it.
zh: 那六个月既是我们的生产力巅峰,也许也是我们的决心巅峰,因为我们必须成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, man, that sounds like just...
zh: 噢，伙计，这听起来简直……

speaker: Unknown
en: Both an incredible time and an incredibly hard time.
zh: 既是一段不可思议的时光，也是一段极其艰难的时光。

speaker: Unknown
en: Incredibly stressful, for sure.
zh: 绝对压力山大。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you set this deadline.
zh: 所以你设定了这个截止日期。

speaker: Unknown
en: The night before you're ready to launch Replit Agent, what are you thinking?
zh: 在准备推出 Replit Agent 的前一天晚上，你在想什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you feeling?
zh: 你有什么感觉？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you confident it's going to work?
zh: 你有信心它能成功吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's going through your head?
zh: 你脑子里在想什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll have to give you all the shameful details about what happened in the couple of days before the launch.
zh: 我得给你们讲讲关于发布会前几天发生的所有丢脸细节。

speaker: Unknown
en: I planned for two different dogfooding sessions with the entire company.
zh: 我计划了两次不同的全公司内部测试会议。

speaker: Unknown
en: 36 hours before launch, literally nothing was working.
zh: 在发布前 36 小时，实际上没有任何东西能正常工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where we had prototypes in the previous days, the product was pretty okay, and it was still very rough on the edges, but was working most of the times.
zh: 在前几天我们还有原型的时候，产品还算过得去，虽然边缘还很粗糙，但大部分时间是能用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we hit...
zh: 然后我们遭遇了……

speaker: Unknown
en: the worst possible planet alignment where we had a few bugs that we couldn't understand where they were.
zh: 最糟糕的行星连珠，我们遇到了几个我们无法理解它们在哪里的 Bug。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it felt very disheartening because I brought in the few people who were not working on the project, including non-technical employees at the company.
zh: 这感觉非常令人沮丧，因为我召集了几个没有参与该项目的人，包括公司里的非技术员工。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I told them, just give this a try.
zh: 我告诉他们，就试试看。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to be amazing.
zh: 这会非常棒的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the experience was awful.
zh: 但体验很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was this close to deciding with Amjad not to launch.
zh: 我当时差点就要决定和 Amjad 不发布了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I told to the core team that was working on Agent, and we said, guys, we're going to pull another all-nighter.
zh: 然后我对负责 Agent 的核心团队说，我们说，伙计们，我们要再通个宵。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to get to the bottom of this.
zh: 我们要把这事搞清楚。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to find out what happened.
zh: 我们要找出发生了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we have another 36 hours to do it.
zh: 我们还有 36 小时来做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fast forward, I think, 16 hours from that moment, we did another real footing session.
zh: 快进，我觉得是 16 小时后，我们进行了另一次真实的内部测试会议。

speaker: Unknown
en: The product was finally working to much surprise of everyone at the company.
zh: 令人惊讶的是，产品终于能用了，这让公司所有人都大吃一惊。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we said, OK, tomorrow morning.
zh: 我们说，好吧，明天早上。

speaker: Unknown
en: STEPHANIE WONG- And what does finally working mean?
zh: STEPHANIE WONG- 所谓的终于能用是什么意思？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, what was it doing?
zh: 比如，它在做什么？

en: So I think especially for the non-technical employees at Replit, it was the first time that they went from a prompting natural language to a very basic application showing up in front of their eyes without doing anything different.
zh: 所以我认为，特别是对于 Replit 的非技术员工来说，这是他们第一次从输入自然语言提示词到一个非常基本的应用程序出现在他们眼前，而不需要做任何不同的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And those are folks that never wrote a single line of code in their lives, even though they were working at Replit.
zh: 这些人甚至一辈子都没写过一行代码，尽管他们在 Replit 工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because the truth is, no matter how much we ask them, please, you should dogfood the product.
zh: 因为事实是，无论我们怎么要求他们，拜托，你们应该内部使用该产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Learning how to write code is not an easy endeavor.
zh: 学习写代码不是一件容易的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of them have very busy lives.
zh: 而且他们中的许多人生活都很忙碌。

speaker: Unknown
en: They work, they have families.
zh: 他们工作，他们有家庭。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're not going to learn how to write code as a side activity.
zh: 他们不会把学习写代码作为一种消遣活动。

speaker: Unknown
en: Suddenly, everyone became a software creator or a rabbit.
